Welcoming immigrants and building and inclusive library
Body Text:
ALA-identified underserved population groups include refugees and immigrants, rural or isolated communities, historically disadvantaged racial or ethnic groups, LGBTQIA+ teens, people with mental health challenges, and those experiencing homelessness. Serving the Underserved: Strategies for Inclusive Community Engagement outlines a fresh approach to how libraries can think about and effectively reach these groups. You'll discover strategies for identifying information needs where underserved populations are and learn about many successful services, programs, and partnerships. 

Libraries and Sanctuary: Supporting Refugees and Other New Arrivals "has [power] as a conversation starter and foundational text to further continue moving the library and information sector to be a force of emancipation and social justice," says The Journal of Librarianship and Information Science, adding "from individual accounts of asylum, organizational responses, to wider policy documents, this book offers the reader a thoughtful exploration of previous action in a thematic way that builds up from the past, present and into future activities." 

The first of its kind, The Stories We Share: A Guide to PreK–12 Books on the Experience of Immigrant Children and Teens in the United States spotlights dozens of award-winning titles that primarily feature a first- or second-generation immigrant child or teen as a narrator or main character. A valuable tool for teaching, collection development, and readers' advisory, it was named Best Professional Resource for School or Youth Librarians—2019 SLC/ARBA Best of Reference Awards. 

Titles on community inclusion and development.

Subject: Employee Appreciation Day
Body Text:
Track your progress, discover new stories, and inspire a year of reading. 

Employee Appreciation Day is March 7! 
Recognize and Support Library Workers. 

Perfect for spring planning, our newest 12-month, undated reading challenge planner is a great gift for showing your appreciation of employees, colleagues and yourself. Filled with weekly book recommendations drawn from Booklist’s top selections and ALA awards (Carnegie, Printz, Stonewall, Alex Awards), plus journaling prompts, this engagement calendar will challenge and delight readers across genres. It comes complete with reading logs, stickers, monthly and weekly spreads with ample writing space and to-do sections, habit trackers, and more. 

Provide inspiration with Renew Yourself: A Six-Step Plan for More Meaningful Work. The Journal of Hospital Librarianship concludes, "This book will help the new LIS graduate, a mid-career staffer, or a library veteran who is burned out. The author discusses strategies to help a stifled or frustrated worker cope with their existing situation. This is a wonderful work to encourage the reader to learn to flourish and grow in their work life and add meaning to their work life. Highly recommended!" 

Remind employees of the countless ways in which they're making a difference for their communities with Libraryland: It's All about the Story. As one goodreads review puts it, "Right now, during this time of extreme burnout, I feel like this book is essential for public library workers. While there were stories about big projects to inspire readers, my favorite stories were the ones about individual patrons whose lives were improved by visiting a library. What we do and how we treat people matters. I hope we will get more books like this in the future." 

Newly refreshed and updated, Neal-Schuman Library Technology Companion: A Basic Guide for Library Staff, Seventh Edition will give employees at every stage of their career a sound and sensible way to consider, access, and use library technologies to better meet the needs of their patrons and communities. Representing a complete update of the book under a new author, this new edition is bolstered with fresh insights gleaned from librarians and library staff members sharing how they work with a given technology in their library settings.

Technology and Well-Being at Your Library
Body Text:
As AI reshapes how humans learn, work, and interact with information, libraries across the ecosystem—from public to academic, from school to special libraries—must resist the temptation to merely serve as static support and instead claim the center by becoming a dynamic, positive influence. Because, as Generative AI and Libraries: Claiming Our Place in the Center of a Shared Future persuasively argues, libraries are uniquely positioned to lead AI's ethical and human-centered integration within communities. 

One Goodreads reviewer raves, "I was intrigued by the optimism that [authors Chris Rosser and Michael Hanegan] shared on the future of libraries and librarians in the 'Age of Intelligence'—the new world we will inhabit with artificial intelligence and specifically generative AI tools. This book did not disappoint ... Instead of closing the book with pessimism, the authors leave librarians with a pep talk, stating that they have a crucial role to play in the integration of AI in our society if only they are willing to stand in the center and assist their institutions, colleagues, and communities in working together. I, for one, am excited to meet this new challenge!" 

Catch up with the authors' presentation "5 Things Libraries Need to Know and Do about Generative AI" and other tech topics explored during the recent ALA Tech Lists event. 

Does technology have a role to play in supporting the well-being of library staff? Several contributors to Well-Being in the Library Workplace: A Handbook for Managers believe it does, from promoting digital inclusion as a means to reduce loneliness to using technology tools to set healthy work/life boundaries. From editor Bobbi L. Newman's essential guide, readers will learn a variety of concrete steps for creating and maintaining a supportive, productive work environment. 

Feeling burned out or in need of a refresh? June's virtual event "Wellness and Stress Reduction Tips for Library Workers" put the spotlight on looking after yourself, offering an insightful hour of self-care tips and expert advice. And claim an additional respite with our free downloadable coloring pages and writing prompts.

Body Text:
ALA Editions invites anyone seeking top-notch tips for building digital accessibility and literacy to join us Wednesday, December 3, 2025 at 12 PM ET/11 AM CT, when we'll present the two-part webinar Planning for Digital Accessibility and Literacy in 2026 over the course of an hour. The presenting authors' session descriptions follow below: 

Part 1 - presented by Carli Spina and Rebecca Albrecht Oling, authors of The Digital Accessibility Handbook for Libraries 

With new rules under Title II of the ADA starting to take effect in April 2026, now is the time for libraries to think critically about the accessibility of their online presence. While this can feel overwhelming, there are straightforward steps you can take to improve digital accessibility. In this session, we will give you concrete tools and techniques to make accessibility improvements quickly. You'll leave with immediate steps you can apply at any library. 

Part 2 - presented by Jenna Kammer and Lauren Hays, authors of Digital Literacy in Public Libraries 

In this session, we will describe ways in which libraries of all types (academic, public, school, special, etc.) can plan for digital literacy. These strategies will focus on embedding digital literacy into existing library programs, as well as designing new opportunities. As digital tools continue to evolve, librarians can support use and access to these tools.

Inclusive Cataloging: Histories, Context, and Reparative Approaches 

Get inspiration and actionable guidance for equitable cataloging with Inclusive Cataloging: Histories, Context, and Reparative Approaches, published by ALA Editions in partnership with Core — ALA's membership division for technical services, library technology, and library management. 

This book offers an expansive re-examination of traditional cataloging to show how metadata practices can reinforce bias, while also sharing practical and reparative alternatives. Catalogue & Index praises it as "an ideal guide for metadata professionals or anyone interested in cataloging through an equity lens" that will "leave you with the feeling that it is possible to do something, whether that be individually or collectively, and now is the perfect time to do so."

Subject: Foster well-being at your library and beyond
Body Text:
Well-Being in the Library Workplace 
A Handbook for Managers 

Learn concrete steps for creating and maintaining a supportive, productive work environment that nurtures well-being among library staff. 

"No matter your management style or where you sit on the management org chart, this gift of managerial wisdom is a keeper … This sagacious compilation will benefit library managers whether they read it cover to cover relaxing at home or dive into when, to their utter astonishment, things quiet down for a few moments during their hectic workday." 
— Booklist 

"Offers 18 chapters filled with valuable insights from frontline professionals … This important work should be part of every supervisor's toolkit to help improve their own management skills, empower their staff, and promote a robust, responsive workplace culture. Appropriate for small and large public and academic libraries seeking to better manage organizational health." 
— Library Journal (starred review) 

Navigating Difficult Situations in Public Libraries 
The PLA Guide to Trauma-Informed De-Escalation 

Build micro-skills for handling difficult situations with trauma-informed strategies. 

"What a great resource! Before I went into librarianship, I was a social worker, and this book bridges the two fields in a straightforward way. It discusses the effects of trauma on both library workers and their patrons. It includes practical, actionable advice like statements and wording to use with patrons in crisis. There are helpful worksheets and reference guides as well." 
— L. Graulich (reader review) 

Library staff and administration do more than simply point people toward books and information — we foster well-being for ourselves and others. One way to promote well-being is by tapping into the entrepreneurial spirit and applying it within the library organization — starting with the end in mind, tapping dignity, unity, and harmony in our thinking and daily activities, and creatively reducing bureaucracy. 

Core's February 4 webinar (1:00 pm CST) "Transform and Thrive: Fostering Well-Being" draws out the best thinking on well-being, mindfulness, and catching the entrepreneurial spirit to fill our daily activity with enthusiasm, goodwill, and calmness. Presenter Dorothy Stoltz will share insights that will help you optimize planning and prioritizing, increase the quality of community engagement, and discover better service solutions. Discover how to foster well-being and promote self-renewal. 

Starting at just $44.50, this 60-minute webinar will show you how to activate creative thinking and enrich daily activities in practical ways. Register today.
